findings.title: Calendar/video cleanup is not awaited on reschedule
findings.body: getCalendar is now async, but the new await sits inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not wait for those callbacks, and the surrounding try/catch cannot see rejections from them. Reschedule therefore marks the booking cancelled, sends the reschedule email, and returns true while calendar deleteEvent / deleteMeeting are still in flight. On a serverless runtime the process can freeze before those calls finish, so the old calendar event and meeting are left behind and failures become unhandled rejections.

findings.title: Calendar/video cleanup is not awaited on reschedule
findings.body: Same as the vital reschedule path: await getCalendar was added inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). The caller never waits for those promises, so cancellation of the previous calendar event and video meeting races the email send and the function return. Errors from getCalendar or deleteEvent are not caught by the try/catch, and a short-lived request can exit before the external events are actually deleted.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
findings.body: requestReschedule now uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await getCalendar, then continues immediately to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks. The deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are never collected or awaited, so a reschedule can be reported as done while the previous calendar event and meeting still exist. Rejections from the dynamic import or the provider call are unhandled.

findings.title: Recurring calendar deletes are pushed after the await set is already consumed
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining occurrences, credentials are walked with forEach(async ...) and getCalendar is awaited before calendar.deleteEvent. The resulting promises are pushed onto apiDeletes only after that await. Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) later in the handler therefore often runs while apiDeletes is still empty, so those deletes are not part of the awaited set. The handler can return, and a serverless isolate can exit, before recurring calendar events are removed.

findings.title: Every app import() starts immediately and can reject unhandled
findings.body: Each import() is invoked while evaluating the appStore object, so loading this module starts every app package at once and does not load an app only when it is used. A rejection is only handled if some caller later awaits that specific key. Any app whose promise rejects before it is awaited (failed module, missing dependency) is an unhandled rejection and can crash the Node process, even for a request that never touches that app.
